canonical_claim: `GC REBUILD` shares `SYSTEM_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GARBAGE_COLLECTION` with regular GC, so the current access model cannot grant the two operations independently.
Invoking SQL `GC REBUILD` without a disk writes `gc/state` on every CA disk on the node, so requiring an explicit disk is a tracked safety/usability improvement.
The base `CasSingleWriterSlot` renewal and foreign-touch failure paths have no gtest coverage and need a backend token-displacement test plus a crash-path test.
The background `CasGcScheduler` pacing loop and its error-swallow behavior have no dedicated gtest coverage.
Async-insert retry row loss from the dedup-token-versus-part hazard is documented but has no gtest; the soak defaults to `async_insert=0`.

The `GcSnapPersist` event value and `gc_snap_persist` string have only an enum declaration and string case, with no emitter or reader; persisted numeric ordinal compatibility must be checked before removal.
The Build event's `UInt64 round` field is written as zero at five `CasBuild.cpp` sites because round is no longer a writer concept; consumers must be checked before removing it.
`folded_cursor` remains load-bearing for part-manifest folding but is a vestigial zero only on the ref-intake path, where `snap_generation` and `snap_attempt` supersede it.
The `retired_refs` map described in `Core/CasGcFormats.h` may be stale after retired-in-snapshot; its live field and population must be verified before removal.
The legacy `{writer_epoch,build_sequence}` pair in `Core/CasManifestId.h` survives the snapshot-plus-log ref model and needs an architecture-store audit to determine whether it can be reduced.
Ack-floor round soak validation is still required for a writer hard-killed during a commit burst, a paused writer holding the floor, and a request-count guard for O(delta)+O(servers) behavior.
`Resolved::manifest_size` is always zero because `CasStore::resolveRef` never sets it; this is tracked as the minor B10 gap.

The TOKEN-implies-CONTENT startup probe is an open item because adding it to the backend contract has design value but may add surface; it is a candidate only if it can be implemented as a pure Ring-0 addition to the existing `Cas::Probe` battery.
A future §5 revival would require a faithful split-action two-leader TLA+ model and a token-preserving `adoptEvidence` recovery action.
The superseded design required verifying that the receiver's `min_active_fn_` covers an in-flight fetch/relink build for the entire fetch; this was its single stated integration point.
The triage backlog defers the fetch-handoff pin for №6, a GC backstop for empty ownerless Live namespaces for №11, and `casAppendObject` for №26 until a concurrent appender is introduced.
The narrower hazard in which a block-id outlives a durably committed part that is lost later remains a separate pre-existing concern; verify-on-dedup is the candidate mitigation.

The S38 clamp-liveness gap requires the clamp path to emit a late-log report even when the corresponding sweep is suppressed; it was escalated as a HARD backlog item rather than treated as a regression.

The parallel-write plan leaves the 500-partition benchmark and BACKLOG write-path entry unresolved until `CasRefBatchFlushes` is much less than `CasRefBatchedMutations`, queue wait falls sharply, and measured wall time improves.

The remaining Part B coverage gap includes gate-0 cases for `Deleting`, absent parts, other-disk matches, `Deleting → Outdated` rollback, and same-name `MOVE ... TO DISK`; the integration battery that was declared to own these cases covered none of them.

The remaining confirm test gaps include recovery that omitted one `LIST` record, an ambiguous append during abort cleanup, zero or multiple routing matches, source remount between offer and confirm, and HTTP-level transport failure or absent answers.

The read-side fix for read-created catalog entries is to resolve a namespace without creating one and return an optional life only when the namespace exists and its files are readable; the decision was to be made before the removal lifecycle.

The mismatch hazard requires a detector that records names seen at dead incarnations and raises an anomaly when the current incarnation contributes neither a listed ref object nor `_ckpt`; the authority-only predicate does not cover this case.

`[RECOVER-REF-TABLE-LIST-RESIDUAL]` remains open because `recoverRefTableDetailed` and `recoverRefTable` recover by full LIST plus replay while the production mount path and fsck `checkRefStream` walk arithmetically; the affected consumers include fsck replay, orphan-manifest deletion premises, `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD`, and fsck dangle revalidation.

`CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore` is the next LIST-trust audit target: its `listedTok` discovery comes from LIST and gates a Phase-2 skip that advances the durable cursor without source edges, so v9's effect on that premise remains unanswered.; The `listedTok` premise has no recorded verdict and `CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore_RESULTS.md` is absent; the model's use of a LIST-derived token as a durable-coverage skip condition requires an explicit audit result.

The post-restart approximately 949/s window exceeded the serial 327/s ceiling, so it remains unresolved whether some fold paths are concurrent or whether warm connections, edge mix, or cached bodies changed the conditions; this determines whether removing HEAD buys about 2x everywhere.

The remaining GC scalability priority is to eliminate the per-round pool enumeration used by `defer_decision`; the report also identifies sharing that enumeration with `ref_list_probe` as a separate optimization.

The merge-churn-to-CAS-traffic ratio remains open because the required `system.content_addressed_log` and `content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` rows were lost with the containers; it requires manifest counts and repoint traffic per unit of merge churn.

No test currently injects a throwing `casPut` on `refCatalogKey` through the `CasRefCatalog::deleteCompletedRemovingAtSnapshot` attempt-failure branch; adjacent fence-check exception branches are covered, but this CAS-throw branch remains untested.
The namespace-file zero-catalog coverage still lacks the `listDirectory`/`listNamespaceFiles` operation; read, write, remove, append, and rotation are already exercised by the existing profile test.
